title: Aloo Gosht (Pakistani meat and potato curry)

ingredients.name: lamb or mutton on the bone
green chillies and coriander to finish

steps: Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the meat and ginger-garlic paste and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli, coriander, cumin and salt and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes and cook for 20 minutes more until they are soft and the gravy has thickened.
Stir in the garam masala and finish with green chillies and coriander.
Serve with roti or rice.

title: Bannu Pulao (Pashtun spiced beef and rice)

ingredients.name: beef on the bone, cut into pieces
long-grain basmati rice, washed and soaked

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot, fry the onions until deep golden and set about a third aside for topping.
Add the beef, crushed garlic and salt and brown the meat for about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cumin seeds, peppercorns, cardamom, coriander and whole chillies, then cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add 3 cups of water, cover and simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 hour (add a little more water if it dries out).
Spread the soaked rice over the meat, tuck the whole garlic head into the centre, add enough hot water to cover the rice by 1 cm and cook uncovered until the water is absorbed.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to the lowest setting and steam for 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy.
Fluff gently, top with the reserved fried onions and serve with raita and salad.

title: Bun Kebab (Karachi street-food burger)

ingredients.name: shami kebab patties, or beef mince patties

steps: Make the kebab patties (for example from a shami kebab mixture), flatten them and shallow-fry until browned on both sides.
Dip each patty in beaten egg and fry for another minute so it is coated.
Split the buns, toast them on a buttered griddle and spread one side with tamarind chutney and the other with mint chutney.
Lay a patty in each bun with onion and tomato.
Serve hot, wrapped in paper if you like.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chapli Kebab (Pashtun spiced beef patties)
steps: Combine the mince with the onion, tomatoes, chillies, coriander, crushed spices, chilli flakes and salt.
Add the egg and cornflour and knead for a few minutes until the mixture is sticky and holds together; rest it for 30 minutes.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into flat round patties about 1 cm thick and 10 cm wide.
Heat oil about 1 cm deep in a wide pan and fry the patties over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep brown and crisp at the edges and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with naan, sliced tomato and onion and a tangy chutney.

title: Chicken Karahi (Pakistani wok-cooked tomato chicken)

ingredients.name: chicken on the bone, cut into pieces
fresh ginger matchsticks and coriander to finish

steps: Heat the oil in a karahi or deep wok over high heat, add the garlic paste and let it sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken pieces and fry, turning, for 8 to 10 minutes until they lose their raw colour.
Stir in the ginger paste, tomatoes, salt, turmeric and chilli, then cover and cook on medium heat until the tomatoes collapse into a pulp.
Uncover and keep cooking, mashing the tomatoes with a spoon, until the oil separates and the chicken is nearly tender.
Add the yoghurt, cumin, coriander, black pepper and slit green chillies and cook on high heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the sauce clings thickly to the chicken.
Finish with ginger matchsticks and chopped coriander and serve straight from the pan with hot naan or roti.

title: Dahi Bhalla (lentil dumplings in spiced yoghurt)

ingredients.name: tamarind chutney and mint chutney, to serve

steps: Drain the soaked dal and grind with a splash of water to a thick, fluffy batter, then whisk well for 2 minutes and mix in the salt and cumin.
Heat oil in a pan and drop in spoonfuls of batter, frying until golden, then lift out.
Soak the fried bhallas in warm salted water for 10 minutes and press gently to squeeze out the water.
Whisk the yoghurt with the sugar until smooth and arrange the bhallas on a plate.
Spoon the yoghurt over, then add tamarind and mint chutneys and sprinkle with cumin powder, chilli and chaat masala.

title: Doodh Pati Chai (Pakistani milk tea)
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan with the crushed cardamom.
Add the tea leaves and simmer for 2 minutes until the water darkens.
Pour in the milk and sugar and bring back to a boil, then lower the heat.
Let it simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tea is deep amber and creamy.
Strain into cups and serve hot with biscuits or rusk.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Falooda (Pakistani rose milk with vermicelli and ice cream)

ingredients.name: basil seeds (sabja), soaked in water for 15 minutes
vanilla or pistachio kulfi or ice cream
chopped pistachios and almonds, to top

steps: Stir the sugar and half the rose syrup into the cold milk until dissolved and chill well.
Put a spoonful of the remaining rose syrup in the bottom of each tall glass.
Add the soaked basil seeds and the cooked vermicelli in layers.
Pour the cold rose milk over, then top each glass with a scoop of kulfi or ice cream.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts and serve right away with a long spoon.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Gola Ganda (Pakistani shaved ice with syrups)
steps: Simmer the sugar and water to a clear syrup and cool, then divide into portions and flavour with different syrups and the lime juice.
Shave the ice finely in a blender or ice shaver and pack firmly onto sticks or into cups.
Pour the coloured syrups generously over the ice so they soak through.
Drizzle with condensed milk and add a pinch of chaat masala if you like a savoury edge.
Eat immediately before it melts.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Haleem (Pakistani spiced meat and lentil porridge)

ingredients.name: yellow split peas or moong dal
fried onions, lemon, ginger matchsticks, green chilli, coriander and chaat masala to serve

steps: Fry half the onions in half the ghee until golden, add the meat and ginger-garlic paste and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the chilli powder, turmeric, salt and the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Add the drained wheat, all the lentils and the rice, and continue to simmer, stirring often, for another 1.5 to 2 hours until everything has broken down into a thick mass.
Beat the pot vigorously with a wooden spoon or masher until the meat shreds into the grains and the haleem is smooth and stretchy, adding hot water if it is too stiff.
Fry the remaining onions in the remaining ghee until dark golden, stir in the garam masala and pour this tarka over the haleem.
Serve hot in bowls with fried onions, lemon wedges, ginger matchsticks, chopped chilli, coriander and a pinch of chaat masala.

title: Halwa Poori (Pakistani semolina halwa with puffed bread and chickpeas)

ingredients.name: onion, 1 tomato and spices for the curry

steps: Make the pooris: knead the flour with the salt, oil and warm water into a firm dough and rest for 20 minutes.
For the halwa, toast the semolina in the ghee until fragrant and golden, then carefully add the sugar dissolved in hot water with the cardamom and stir until thick.
For the chana, fry the onion until golden, add the tomato, salt, chilli, turmeric and cumin, then add the chickpeas and 1 cup of water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough into small thin rounds and deep-fry in hot oil, pressing so they puff up, until golden.
Serve the hot pooris with the semolina halwa and the chickpea curry.

title: Kadhi (Sindhi/Punjabi yoghurt and gram flour curry)
steps: Whisk the yoghurt, gram flour, turmeric, salt and water together until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour the mixture into a heavy pot and bring to a boil, stirring continuously.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until the kadhi thickens and the raw gram flour smell has gone.
Heat the oil in a small pan, add the cumin and mustard seeds, curry leaves, chillies, coriander and chilli powder and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Pour the tempering into the kadhi, stir through and serve with plain rice or roti.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Makki di Roti (Punjabi maize flour flatbread)

ingredients.name: plain flour or atta (optional, helps binding)

steps: Mix the maize flour, plain flour, salt and carom seeds in a bowl.
Add warm water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough that does not crack when pressed.
Divide into 6 balls and flatten each between oiled palms or on a sheet of baking paper to about 2 mm thick, patting gently to keep the edges from splitting.
Heat a griddle or tawa on medium heat and cook each roti for 2 to 3 minutes per side until brown spots appear.
Brush with ghee and serve hot with sarson da saag, white butter and jaggery.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Nihari (Pakistani slow-cooked beef stew)

ingredients.name: beef shank, cut into large chunks
fresh ginger matchsticks, green chillies and lemon to serve

steps: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until deep golden brown, then lift out about a third and set aside for garnish.
Add the beef, ginger paste and garlic paste and fry on a high flame for 5 to 6 minutes until the meat is sealed and browned.
Stir in the chilli powder, turmeric, ground fennel, dry ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and salt, and cook the spices for a couple of minutes, sprinkling in a splash of water if they stick.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the gravy is rich and glossy.
Mix the flour with a little cold water to a smooth slurry, stir it into the stew and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until thickened to a coating consistency.
Stir in the garam masala and, if you like, spoon a little hot ghee over the top.
Serve hot with naan, topped with the reserved onions, ginger matchsticks, green chilli and a squeeze of lemon.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Noon Chai (Kashmiri pink salted tea)

ingredients.name: crushed almonds and pistachios, to serve

steps: Boil the water with the tea leaves and baking soda for 10 minutes, stirring and ladling to aerate until the liquid turns a deep red-brown.
Add a small cup of cold water to help bring out the colour, then boil for 5 more minutes.
Pour in the milk, add the salt and cardamom and keep boiling, ladling the tea up and down, until it turns a rosy pink.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes more, strain and serve hot, topped with crushed nuts.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Paya (Pakistani slow-cooked trotter curry)

ingredients.name: ginger matchsticks, green chillies, coriander and lemon to serve

steps: Boil the cleaned trotters in plenty of water for 10 minutes, discard the water and rinse the trotters to remove scum.
Fry the onions in the oil in a large pot until golden, then add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the trotters, chilli, turmeric, coriander, cumin, yoghurt, cardamom and salt and fry for 10 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on very low heat for 5 to 6 hours (or about 1 hour in a pressure cooker) until the meat is soft and the broth is thick and slightly gelatinous.
Stir in the garam masala and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Serve hot with naan, topped with ginger, chillies, coriander and lemon juice.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sai Bhaji (Sindhi spinach and lentil curry)
steps: Heat the oil in a pot, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then fry the onion until soft.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomato, turmeric, chilli, coriander and salt and cook until pulpy.
Add the drained chana dal, potato and 2 cups of water, cover and simmer until the dal is almost tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and dill, cover and cook for 10 minutes more until everything is soft.
Mash lightly with the back of a spoon so the vegetables and dal blend into a thick, creamy curry.
Serve with rice or flatbread.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sajji (Balochi roast leg of lamb)

ingredients.name: leg of lamb or whole chicken (lamb traditional)
cooked rice for the stuffing or side

steps: Prick the lamb all over with a fork so the marinade can penetrate.
Rub the meat with the salt, pepper, cumin, garlic, papaya paste and a little oil, then marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 180 C, place the lamb on a rack over a tray and roast for 2 to 2.5 hours, basting with oil every 30 minutes, until deeply browned and tender.
If you prefer the traditional open-fire effect, finish under a hot grill for 5 minutes to crisp the surface.
Rest for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the rice mixed with fried raisins and almonds and flatbread.

title: Samosa (Pakistani spiced potato pastry)

ingredients.name: oil or ghee for the dough

steps: Rub the flour, salt, carom seeds and 4 tablespoons of oil together, then add water to make a stiff dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Fry the cumin seeds briefly in a little oil, add the potatoes, peas, coriander, chilli, chaat masala and green chillies and cook for 5 minutes, crushing the potatoes lightly.
Roll the dough into thin ovals, halve them and form each half into a cone, seal the edge with water.
Fill each cone with the potato mixture and seal the top firmly.
Fry in medium-hot oil over low-medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve with tamarind or mint chutney.

title: Sarson da Saag (Punjabi mustard greens)
steps: Put the mustard greens, spinach, ginger, half the garlic and the green chillies in a pot with a splash of water and cook, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes until very soft.
Add the maize flour mixed with a little water and cook for 10 more minutes, stirring, to thicken.
Mash or blend the greens briefly so the saag is thick and a little coarse, then season with salt.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, fry the onion and remaining garlic until golden, and stir into the saag.
Serve hot topped with a knob of butter alongside makki di roti.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Seekh Kebab (Pakistani spiced minced meat skewers)

ingredients.name: small onion, grated and squeezed dry

steps: Mix the mince with the onion, ginger-garlic paste, chillies, coriander, spices, gram flour and salt and knead well for several minutes until sticky.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour so the flavours settle.
Wet your hands and press handfuls of the mixture around flat metal or soaked wooden skewers into long sausage shapes.
Grill over charcoal or under a hot grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning and brushing with a little oil, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with naan, onion rings, mint chutney and lemon.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Shab Deg (Pakistani turnips and meat stew)

ingredients.name: lamb or mutton on the bone
turnips, peeled and cut into large pieces

steps: Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the meat and ginger-garlic paste and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, yoghurt, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander and salt and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the meat is nearly tender.
Add the turnips and green chillies and continue to cook for 20 to 25 minutes until the turnips are soft but not breaking.
Stir in the garam masala, rest the pot for 5 minutes and serve with roti or naan.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Shahi Tukray (Pakistani royal fried bread pudding)

ingredients.name: white bread, crusts removed and cut into triangles

steps: Shallow-fry the bread triangles in hot oil or ghee until golden and crisp on both sides, and drain well.
Simmer the milk with the sugar, cardamom and saffron for 20 to 25 minutes until it has reduced by about a third.
Stir in the condensed milk and cream and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Arrange the fried bread in a shallow dish in a single layer and pour the hot milk mixture over it so it soaks in.
Chill for at least an hour or serve warm, topped with the chopped nuts and a little extra cream.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Shami Kebab (Pakistani lentil and meat patties)

ingredients.name: coriander, mint and green chillies, finely chopped

steps: Put the meat, dal, onion, garlic, ginger, red chillies, cumin, garam masala and salt in a pot with the water and simmer until the meat is tender and the water has almost dried up.
Grind the mixture to a smooth, thick paste in a food processor and let it cool.
Mix in the egg and the chopped herbs and chillies, then shape into small round patties.
Shallow-fry the patties in hot oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned and crisp.
Serve with chutney or tucked into bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sheer Khurma (Eid vermicelli milk pudding)
steps: Heat the ghee in a large pan and fry the nuts and raisins briefly until golden, then remove and set aside.
In the same ghee toast the vermicelli for a minute until it darkens a shade.
Add the milk and cardamom and bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the vermicelli is soft.
Stir in the dates, sugar and saffron and simmer for 10 minutes more until the pudding is creamy and lightly thickened.
Stir in half the fried nuts, serve warm or chilled and decorate with the rest.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sheermal (saffron-flavoured sweet flatbread)

ingredients.name: saffron soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

steps: Mix the flour, salt, sugar, yeast and cardamom and rub in 2 tablespoons of the ghee.
Add the warm milk gradually to make a soft dough, knead for 8 minutes and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 6 balls, roll into thick discs and prick all over with a fork.
Bake at 220 C for 10 to 12 minutes until lightly golden.
Brush with the saffron milk and remaining ghee as they come out, and serve warm.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sindhi Biryani (spicy Sindhi layered rice with meat)

ingredients.name: lamb or mutton, cut into pieces

steps: Fry the onions in oil until deep brown, remove half and set aside, then add the meat and ginger-garlic paste and fry until sealed.
Stir in the yoghurt, tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, biryani masala, chillies and salt and cook until the meat is almost tender and the masala is thick.
Fry the potatoes separately until lightly golden and add them with the plums to the meat.
Boil the rice in salted water with a few whole spices until 70 percent cooked, then drain.
Layer half the rice over the meat, scatter the herbs and reserved onions, then add the remaining rice and a splash of hot water.
Cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat for 20 to 25 minutes until the rice is tender and everything is fragrant.
Gently mix from the bottom and serve with raita.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sohan Halwa (Pakistani sweet nut brittle)
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the water in a heavy pan, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes until it is a light syrup, stirring in the saffron.
Stir the toasted flour with the milk to a smooth slurry, then slowly stir it into the syrup, whisking so no lumps form.
Add the ghee gradually, a little at a time, stirring constantly over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the mixture is thick, glossy and pulls away from the pan.
Stir in the cardamom and half the nuts.
Pour into a greased tray, smooth the top, scatter the remaining nuts and press them in.
Let it cool and set, then cut into pieces.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Taftan (Pakistani saffron-milk leavened bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl and add the milk, yoghurt, oil, egg and saffron milk.
Knead into a soft dough for 8 minutes and let it rise in a covered bowl for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 6 portions and roll or stretch each into a round, pressing the centre a little thinner.
Prick the surface with a fork, brush with milk and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake on a hot oven tray or pizza stone at 230 C for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Serve warm with nihari or korma.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Zarda (sweet saffron rice)

ingredients.name: orange or yellow food colour, or 1 pinch saffron in 2 tbsp milk

steps: Boil the rice in plenty of water with a pinch of salt until about 80 percent cooked, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot, add the cardamom and cloves and fry for 30 seconds.
Add the sugar with 1/2 cup of water and stir until dissolved and syrupy, then add the colour or saffron.
Layer the rice into the syrup with the raisins, nuts and coconut and make a few holes to let steam escape.
Cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and has absorbed the sweet syrup.
Fluff gently and serve warm or at room temperature.
